answer:
Headline results for run /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (read-only report; no PBS jobs submitted, hazard.py not run):

Records analysed: 759 (stride 20, covering 2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z, 3.314% of the time window).
Anomalous records (|robust z| > 5): 57.
DAS detections: 62 in 53 records; relative b = 0.9849 (34 above Mc).
Pumping: injected 4.654e+05 m3, extracted 5.059e+05 m3, net -4.048e+04 m3 over 15.96 days.
Catalogue: 5 events, ML -0.48 to 0.07 (GDR 859, LBNL/NCEDC March 2016).

CALIBRATED probability (catalogue-based, Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5 — the LBNL catalogue):
  b = 1.0:  Sigma = -5.449, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.0001198, P(M>=5.5) observed volume = 5.236e-06, P(M>=3)/yr = 0.03719
  b = 0.73: Sigma = -5.319, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.004922,  P(M>=5.5) observed volume = 0.0002155, P(M>=3)/yr = 0.2809
  b = 0.65: Sigma = -5.281, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.01474,   P(M>=5.5) observed volume = 0.0006484, P(M>=3)/yr = 0.4653

UPPER BOUND (DAS-based, uncalibrated magnitudes — every detection counted as an event at or above the catalogue Mc, so it over-counts):
  b = 0.9849, Sigma = -2.698, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842

Which is which: the per-b table above is the CALIBRATED estimate, derived from the LBNL/NCEDC earthquake catalogue (GDR 859, March 2016). The single DAS-based figure (b = 0.9849, Sigma = -2.698, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842) is the UPPER BOUND: DAS magnitudes are uncalibrated and every DAS detection is counted as an event at or above the catalogue magnitude of completeness, so it over-counts and is not calibrated.

Bottom line: even under the conservative calibrated catalogue-based estimate, the annual probability of a Pohang-like Mw >= 5.5 event at Brady Hot Springs in March 2016 is small (1.2e-4 to 1.5e-2 per year depending on b), while the DAS-based upper bound (0.078/yr) is roughly 5x to 650x higher and should be treated only as an upper limit.
